title: Merging Dictionaries
hints: Dictionaries have a method that merges another dictionary and resolves key clashes.
`merging(_:uniquingKeysWith:)` takes a function `(old, new) -> value` — an operator can be that function.
jsBridge: JS `{...a, ...b}` makes b win on conflicts. Swift's `merging(_:uniquingKeysWith:)` makes you decide with a closure: `+` to add, `{ $1 }` for "new wins". Merging never silently discards data.

compass.q: `{...a, ...b}` silently overwrites. How does Swift make conflict resolution explicit?
`merging` (returns new) vs `merge` (mutating): when does the mutating version save work?
What does `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` do on a duplicate key? Why is that a crash and not an error?
Merging local and remote settings: which side should win, and should that be a closure parameter?
